results.reason: Identifies the asymmetric §13.2 assignment right: Supplier may assign without consent or notice, including to a competitor, while Customer needs consent. Explains the risk to supply continuity and to confidential specifications, and proposes mutual consent language with a competitor carve-out.

Identifies the §13.3 requirement for Supplier's prior written consent and the termination right. Ties it to the pending sale and recommends deleting or narrowing the clause (competitor-only, consent not unreasonably withheld) or obtaining a waiver before signing or closing.

Identifies the Order Form §2.2 automatic three-year renewal with a 30-day notice window and explains the lock-in risk. Recommends a 120–180 day window, a one-year renewal term, or renewal by mutual agreement only.

Identifies the §9.3 carve-out of Customer's §10.1 indemnity from the cap as one-way, leaving Customer uncapped while Supplier stays capped. Recommends deleting §9.3 or making the carve-out mutual with a separate cap.
Correctly states the prior-12-months fees cap (§9.1), Delaware law (§12.1), and a three-year Initial Term from March 1, 2026.

States the §1.3 order of precedence (Supply Agreement, then Order Form, then Specifications Schedule) and analyzes whether it affects the renewal provision, concluding the issue is a gap rather than a conflict.
Includes a priority table ordered from first to last to raise, with change of control and the uncapped indemnity ranked High at positions 1 and 2.
Each issue is structured with location, what it says, why it matters, and a recommended fix with proposed language. Ends with a separate open questions and business decisions section.
States the Specifications Schedule raises no issue and cites no external statutes or cases. The minor note on entity details is framed as a confirmation request, not an invented issue.
